findings.title: Application role can disable the DB immutability triggers
findings.problem: The same runtime principal that appends DHF records can remove the trigger-based protections that enforce session immutability.
findings.why_it_matters: This makes the append-only/audit-integrity guarantee dependent on application goodwill rather than database policy. A compromised app or bad deployment can rewrite history.
findings.proposed_fix: Run the orchestrator under a DML-only role with no DDL, `DROP TRIGGER`, or `ALTER TABLE` privileges. Reserve migrations and trigger changes for a separate admin role and restate the trust boundary accordingly.

findings.title: API secret is sent in the WebSocket subprotocol header
findings.problem: The full credential is placed in a standard upgrade header that reverse proxies, edge platforms, APM tooling, and diagnostics commonly log. Suppressing the echoed response does not prevent request-side leakage.
findings.why_it_matters: A leaked header exposes a long-lived tenant credential and allows unauthorized orchestrator access.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the credential to an `Authorization` or custom header on the upgrade request. If that is impossible, issue a short-lived one-time token over HTTPS and use that in the upgrade instead; also define mandatory request-header redaction.

findings.title: Same-epoch reconnect behavior conflicts with immutable session metadata
findings.evidence: SPEC-01: same `AddinSessionId` reconnect must "accept the updated capability fields (`AddinVersion`, `SwVersion`, `SwBuild`, `ScreenshotRootPath`)". SPEC-04: "All columns in `dhf.sessions` except `ended_at`, `locked_at`, and `lock_reason` are immutable once inserted."
findings.problem: The contract says reconnects may change capability metadata, but the persistence contract forbids updating the session row, and some named fields are not shown as mutable persisted fields anywhere.
findings.why_it_matters: Implementers have no valid place to put the accepted updates. Either reconnects fail against the immutability trigger or the updated data is silently discarded.
findings.proposed_fix: Choose one contract: either reject same-epoch reconnects when capability fields differ, or add a separate mutable reconnect-metadata store outside the immutable session row and reference it consistently.

findings.title: RecoveryEventContext is not persisted as structured recovery data
findings.evidence: `RecoveryEventContext` defines `Trigger`, `Strategy`, `Success`, `FailureReason`, and `ModelStateDivergenceDescription`, but §7.2 converts them into `var description = "Recovery event: trigger=..."` and writes that into `RawTranscript` via `DhfTurnContext`.
findings.problem: The recovery event contract defines structured fields, but the append path collapses them into free text instead of storing them in structured form.
findings.why_it_matters: Viewer logic, validation, reporting, and audit queries cannot reliably consume or filter recovery outcomes from an ad-hoc string.
findings.proposed_fix: Add recovery-specific persisted fields or a hashed JSONB payload on `dhf.entries`, include them in hash coverage, and expose them in read DTOs. `AppendRecoveryEventAsync` should write the structured fields directly, not stringify them.

findings.title: Recovery screenshot bytes are defined but never written
findings.location: SPEC-04 changelog; SPEC-04 §5 RecoveryEventContext; SPEC-04 §7.2 AppendRecoveryEventAsync
findings.evidence: Migration 008 adds `screenshot_before_png`/`screenshot_after_png`; `RecoveryEventContext` includes `byte[]? ScreenshotBeforePng`/`ScreenshotAfterPng`; §7.2 builds a `DhfTurnContext` with `ScreenshotBeforePath = null` and `ScreenshotAfterPath = null` and never passes the PNG byte arrays.
findings.problem: The append path discards the new recovery screenshot payloads.
findings.why_it_matters: The stated R1 fix is incomplete: deep validation and viewer rendering still cannot rely on recovery-event screenshots being present.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend the append contract so recovery events write `ScreenshotBeforePng` and `ScreenshotAfterPng` into `dhf.entries`, or use a dedicated recovery insert path that persists both hashes and bytes.

findings.title: Heartbeat closure uses an invalid WebSocket close code
findings.evidence: "Missed pong → close with 1006 (\"abnormal closure\") after 2 missed intervals."
findings.problem: Close code 1006 is reserved for local observation and must not be sent in a WebSocket close frame.
findings.why_it_matters: Clients and libraries may reject or misreport the shutdown, and test expectations based on a sent 1006 are invalid.
findings.proposed_fix: Either terminate the connection without sending a close frame and classify it locally as 1006, or send a valid close code with documented semantics.

findings.title: Unknown message-type handling is internally inconsistent
findings.location: SPEC-01 §3 Malformed JSON handling; SPEC-02 §6.5 MessageDispatcher
findings.evidence: SPEC-01 §3 says an "unrecognized" polymorphic discriminator MUST produce `MalformedEnvelope`. SPEC-02 §6.5 says unknown `IClientMessage` subtypes produce `AddinProtocolErrorMessage(ErrorCode = UnknownMessageType)`.
findings.problem: The specs assign two different wire-level outcomes to the same condition.
findings.why_it_matters: Interop tests, retry logic, and diagnostics cannot be implemented deterministically because the receiver behavior depends on which section an implementer followed.
findings.proposed_fix: Define one mapping for each case: e.g. missing/invalid envelope -> `MalformedEnvelope`; well-formed envelope with unsupported `type` -> `UnknownMessageType`. Update all sections and required tests to match.

findings.title: Message-size control has no defined failure path when reduction still does not fit
findings.location: SPEC-01 §7.1 Screenshot transport; SPEC-02 §7.2 Dimension Reduction Strategy
findings.evidence: SPEC-01 requires the add-in to reduce screenshot dimensions until the 2 MiB cap fits. SPEC-02 limits this to "Iterative halving up to 4 iterations. Abandon after iteration 4."
findings.problem: The contract does not define what message is sent if the screenshot is still too large after four reductions, and it never requires checking the size of the fully serialized `ToolResultMessage` after adding `StateAfter`.
findings.why_it_matters: Oversize screenshot turns can dead-end with no valid wire outcome or still exceed the 4 MiB envelope even after image reduction.
findings.proposed_fix: Define an explicit terminal behavior after max reductions and require a final full-message-size check that can trigger feature-tree truncation or a deterministic failure before send.

findings.title: Planned disconnect leaves behavior undefined after the 60-second escalation timeout
findings.evidence: "Waits for any currently-executing tool call to complete on the UI thread (60-second escalation timeout)."
findings.problem: The spec never states what the add-in does when the currently executing COM call is still running at 60 seconds, even though earlier sections state executing COM cannot be preempted.
findings.why_it_matters: Shutdown and DHF-session-closure behavior diverge precisely in the hard case this timeout is supposed to govern: some implementations will hang, some will force close, and session semantics will differ.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify the exact post-timeout action and resulting DHF/session semantics: continue waiting, skip teardown and leave session open, force process exit, or another single mandated behavior.

top_3_must_fix: Remove DDL/trigger-modification privileges from the runtime DHF role.
Stop sending API secrets in `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` and use a non-loggable auth mechanism for the WebSocket upgrade.
Make recovery events persist structured fields and screenshot bytes instead of flattening/discarding them.
